item.title: New York court reverses $400,000 mortgage foreclosure judgment after years of legal battle following husband’s death
item.description: A recent ruling by an appeals court has overturned a foreclosure decision related to a property in Babylon, New York. The court determined that Bank of America did not give the borrower adequate notice prior to starting foreclosure procedures and failed to show that it had the necessary standing in the case. Consequently, the court rejected the bank's request for a summary judgment against the estate of Alice McNamara.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida man names girl in will despite sperm donor agreement; court denies her claim to house
item.description: A Florida appeals court has upheld the rejection of a young girl's claim to a deceased man's house, despite his having named her in his will. The dispute involved a 2017 sperm donor agreement between Melissa Azrack and Malcolm Dorman. The appeal failed because Azrack did not challenge the lower court's finding that the property was not protected homestead property.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 17-year-old US soldier killed in Korean War identified after 75 years; remained buried as ‘Unknown X-1642’, to be laid to rest in Maryland
item.description: Pvt. Joseph E. Boyd, who went missing in action at just 17 during the Korean War, has finally been identified decades later. His remains, previously known as Unknown X-1642, have been matched to his identity through advanced forensic techniques, including DNA testing. A dignified burial ceremony is set for October 21, 2026, in Owings Mills, Maryland, underscoring the ongoing commitment to honor missing service members from historical conflicts.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Isabel Rossi, 14, whose maths model improved simulated earthquake sensor coverage by 16.7%
item.description: A 14-year-old student from Williamsburg, Virginia, has become one of 30 finalists in a national science competition after developing a mathematical model to improve earthquake sensor placement. Isabel Rossi's six-month research project showed that adding just five sensors could increase simulated detection coverage by 16.7%. She used earthquake records from California and mathematical methods to identify better sensor locations.

item.title: 86-year-old Texas man spent nearly 40 years building 62-foot boat to sail to Alaska; now strangers are raising thousands to help him fulfil his dream
item.description: An 86-year-old man from Mineral Wells, Texas, has been building a 62-foot steel boat since 1987. After three visitors discovered his ambition, they launched a crowdfunding campaign to support the project. More than $41,000 has been raised towards completing the boat and moving it to a launch site. The remaining work on the vessel is expected to require about $50,000 in funding.

item.title: China's Bohai Bay oyster reefs show recovery, with 286 oysters per square metre
item.description: A study of oyster reef restoration in China's Bohai Bay has found encouraging signs of marine habitat recovery between 2022 and 2026. By March 2026, artificial reefs supported an average of 286 oysters per square metre, while suspended particles in the water had declined by approximately 62%. Published in Frontiers in Marine Science, the study also recorded an increase in seabed animals. However, researchers said further monitoring was needed to establish the project's long-term effectiveness.

item.title: Mariska Hargitay helped fund testing of 11,341 rape kits in Detroit; 263 convictions followed
item.description: American actress Mariska Hargitay helped support a project to test 11,341 sexual assault evidence kits discovered in a Detroit police warehouse in 2009. The kits had remained untested for years, with cases dating back to 1984. Led by Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy, the initiative had secured 263 convictions by April 2025, with investigations continuing across the United States.

item.title: Pompeii’s grandest ancient residence gets €1.4 million restoration
item.description: Thanks to a private sponsor, the House of Marcus Fabius Rufus in Pompeii is set for restoration, with a portion expected to welcome guided groups by this Christmas. The renovation focuses on fresco restoration and improved visitor access, addressing the extensive damage the site suffered since its closure in 1980 due to a volcanic eruption.

item.title: Scottish castle built in 1584 with original fireplaces and staircases listed for £120,000
item.description: Baltersan Castle, built in 1584 near Maybole, Ayrshire, is now available on the market for £120,000. This castle, which is roofless and Category A-listed, occupies 0.75 acres of land. Notable figures like Charles Rennie Mackintosh and poets Robert Burns and John Keats have been linked to the property. Although the building retains much of its original structure, planning consent for restoration has expired.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Georgia woman sues over neighbour's marijuana smoke despite smoking ban; court dismisses claim
item.description: A Georgia woman sued after claiming her neighbour’s marijuana smoke repeatedly entered her apartment despite a no-smoking lease, affecting her breathing and health. Bridget Francis alleged that the apartment management ignored her complaints. However, on October 19, 2026, a Georgia appeals court upheld the dismissal of her claims against a California teachers’ pension fund, ruling that it was legally protected from the lawsuit.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California seventh-grader tests potential brain-injury treatment on 350 fruit flies
item.description: Alekha Goldberg from California has distinguished herself as a finalist in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge. Her innovative research focuses on the neuroprotective properties of methylene blue for traumatic brain injury, utilizing fruit flies in her experiments. The results show enhanced climbing ability and survival rates post-injury.

item.title: Maldives sinks two retired aircraft to create an unusual underwater reef; coral restoration begins in 2026
item.description: Two decommissioned Dornier 228 aircraft are submerged near Kudagiri Island to create a diving attraction. Conservation teams are working to establish an artificial reef by attaching coral fragments to underwater frames. The project aims to combine marine tourism with aviation history while promoting coral growth. Various organizations are collaborating to monitor the ecological impact of this initiative.

item.title: Emma Stone’s 1926 LA home sells for $4.3 million after renovation, $305,000 above asking price
item.description: Emma Stone has beautifully transformed a historic home in Los Angeles, which she bought for $2.3 million back in 2019. After completing significant renovations, she listed the property for $3.995 million in January 2024. Boasting a guesthouse, a larger kitchen, and preserved architectural features, the home quickly sold for $4.3 million just ten days later, showcasing Stone’s savvy real estate acumen.
